name: Reconquista: Fall of Toledo
summary: Alfonso VI of Castile captures Toledo, the old Visigothic capital and a major Islamic city, the first major Reconquista victory. Toledo becomes the center of the 12th-century translation movement, where Christian, Jewish, and Muslim scholars translate Arabic philosophical and scientific texts into Latin, bringing Aristotle, Euclid, and Avicenna to Western Europe.

_quarry.structural_significance: Toledo's translation schools are the primary channel through which ancient Greek and medieval Islamic science enter Latin European scholarship; the capture also alarms the Taifa kings enough to invite the Almoravids from North Africa.
